chunks.speaker: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT
chunks.text: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT: MARTA GOMEZ Case: Blackwood Manor Art Heist Interviewer: Detective Reynolds

chunks.speaker: Marta Gomez
chunks.text: Interviewee: Marta Gomez, Evening Housekeeper [11:15 AM] REYNOLDS: Marta, where were you working between 9:00 PM and 11:00 PM? [11:15 AM] GOMEZ: I was cleaning the second-floor gallery and dining room.

chunks.speaker: Marta Gomez
chunks.text: [11:16 AM] REYNOLDS: Did you see Julian Vance during that time? [11:16 AM] GOMEZ: Yes. Julian was not at the security desk. I saw Julian walking near the basement service elevator carrying a heavy black duffel bag around 10:15 PM. [11:17 AM] REYNOLDS: Did the gallery motion sensors go off?

chunks.speaker: Marta Gomez
chunks.text: [11:17 AM] GOMEZ: Yes, the loud acoustic chime in the hallway buzzed at 10:15 PM, but it shut off after thirty seconds.

chunks.speaker: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT
chunks.text: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT: CLARA STERLING Case: Blackwood Manor Art Heist Interviewer: Detective Reynolds

chunks.speaker: Clara Sterling
chunks.text: Interviewee: Clara Sterling, Gallery Curator [09:00 AM] REYNOLDS: State your name and position. [09:00 AM] STERLING: Clara Sterling, chief curator at Blackwood Manor Gallery.

chunks.speaker: Clara Sterling
chunks.text: [09:01 AM] REYNOLDS: When did you last see the Vermeer canvas 'The Silent Witness'? [09:01 AM] STERLING: I personally inspected the vault at 6:00 PM on Friday and locked the biometric vault safe. [09:02 AM] REYNOLDS: Did anyone else have the emergency override code?

chunks.speaker: Clara Sterling
chunks.text: [09:02 AM] STERLING: No, only Lord Blackwood and I possess the vault keys. The security guard, Julian Vance, has no safe access. [09:03 AM] REYNOLDS: What time did you leave the estate? [09:03 AM] STERLING: I drove through the front gates at 6:30 PM and attended a charity dinner in town until midnight.

chunks.speaker: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT
chunks.text: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT: JULIAN VANCE Case: Blackwood Manor Art Heist Interviewer: Detective Reynolds

chunks.speaker: Julian Vance
chunks.text: Interviewee: Julian Vance, Night Guard [10:30 AM] REYNOLDS: Julian, describe your patrol route on Friday night. [10:30 AM] VANCE: I began my shift at 7:00 PM. I stayed in the security control booth until 11:00 PM.

chunks.speaker: Julian Vance
chunks.text: [10:31 AM] REYNOLDS: Did you hear the basement motion alarm at 10:15 PM? [10:31 AM] VANCE: The motion alarm never sounded in the booth. The control panel showed green all night. [10:32 AM] REYNOLDS: Did anyone visit the estate during your watch?

chunks.speaker: Julian Vance
chunks.text: [10:32 AM] VANCE: The courier van from Apex Deliveries arrived at 9:50 PM with conservatory plants, and drove off at 10:30 PM. [10:33 AM] REYNOLDS: Did you leave your desk at all? [10:33 AM] VANCE: I remained at the security console continuously from 7:00 PM to midnight without leaving.

chunks.speaker: SYNOPSIS
chunks.text: SYNOPSIS: At 06:15 AM on October 19, curator Clara Sterling discovered the basement vault door open. The 17th-century Vermeer canvas was cut from its gilded frame and missing. 2.

chunks.speaker: FORCED ENTRY
chunks.text: FORCED ENTRY: No external doors, windows, or gates showed forced entry. Entry was executed via the rear delivery gate and physical vault key. 3.

chunks.speaker: FORENSICS
chunks.text: FORENSICS: Tire tracks in the gravel courtyard match standard commercial light transport vehicles.
